author: Ramamonjiarisoa, Faramalala Mamitiana

steps.title: Collect and label blood sample
steps.instruction: Collect 5 mL of venous blood into a dry Vacutainer tube with a red cap using aseptic technique; gently invert the tube 3–5 times to activate clotting; affix a unique barcoded label and verify that it matches the participant’s study code; register the sample in the LIMS or a paper log, recording the time of venipuncture and any other relevant metadata.

steps.title: Allow clotting and centrifuge serum
steps.instruction: Allow the collected blood to clot at room temperature for 30–60 minutes in an upright position away from direct sunlight or heat sources; centrifuge the clotted blood at 3000 rpm for 10 minutes, ensuring that centrifugation occurs within 6 hours of venipuncture.

steps.title: Inspect, aliquot, and prepare serum for transport
steps.instruction: Visually inspect the centrifuged sample, then carefully aspirate the clear supernatant serum while avoiding red blood cells or buffy coat; transfer approximately 2–3 mL of serum into pre‑labeled cryovials bearing the same unique identifier; check for gross hemolysis or lipemia and record this observation.

steps.title: Transport serum or whole blood under cold chain
steps.instruction: Place the serum cryovials in a sealed, leak‑proof secondary container and then into an insulated cool box with ice packs; maintain a transport temperature of 2–8 °C, monitoring with a thermometer or data logger when possible; ensure the total transport time does not exceed 6 hours. If serum separation cannot be performed on site, transport the primary blood tube (unspun, upright) in the same temperature range, centrifuge and separate serum immediately upon arrival, completing centrifugation within 6–8 hours after venipuncture. If delays are expected to exceed 8 hours, arrange for a nearby hub laboratory to perform centrifugation and do not freeze whole blood. Record transport duration and temperature as pre‑analytical QC indicators.

steps.title: Store serum short‑term or freeze long‑term
steps.instruction: For short‑term storage of less than 48 hours before testing, keep serum at approximately +4 °C in a monitored refrigerator; for long‑term storage, freeze serum aliquots at –80 °C. Prepare multiple aliquots to avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Equilibrate rapid test device and serum
steps.instruction: Bring the rapid test device and any refrigerated serum samples to room temperature before use.

steps.title: Run HIV/syphilis combo rapid test
steps.instruction: Using a calibrated pipette, apply 10 µL of serum to the sample well of the HIV/syphilis combo rapid test; add three drops of the manufacturer‑supplied diluent to the appropriate well; incubate the device at room temperature and read the result after exactly 15 minutes, confirming that the control line is present.

substeps.instruction: If the HIV line is reactive, classify the sample as initially reactive for HIV antibodies and proceed to ELISA confirmation.
If the syphilis line is reactive, classify the sample as initially reactive for syphilis and proceed to the non‑treponemal RPR test.

steps.title: Perform non‑treponemal RPR test
steps.instruction: Place 50 µL of serum onto the designated circle of the RPR card using a pipette; add one drop of RPR antigen according to the manufacturer’s guidelines; gently rotate the card on a mechanical rotator for eight minutes at the recommended speed; after rotation, examine the mixture under adequate lighting for flocculation.

substeps.instruction: A visible flocculation indicates a reactive RPR result and should be confirmed by a treponemal test such as TPHA.
If the RPR is non‑reactive but clinical suspicion is high, consider repeat testing or direct TPHA testing per local guidelines.

steps.title: Conduct treponemal TPHA confirmation
steps.instruction: Dilute the serum 1:80 with the TPHA diluent provided in the kit; dispense 25 µL of the diluted serum into the appropriate test well; add the sensitized erythrocytes (reagent cells) as instructed; incubate the plate for 45–60 minutes at room temperature without disturbance.

substeps.instruction: A diffuse layer of agglutinated cells covering the well surface is interpreted as a positive treponemal result.
A compact “button” of non‑agglutinated cells at the bottom of the well is interpreted as a negative result.

steps.title: Prepare serum dilution for ELISA
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1:21 serum dilution by mixing 10 µL of serum with 200 µL of the assay diluent supplied by the ELISA kit manufacturer; homogenize the mixture gently using a pipette or vortex mixer, avoiding bubble formation.

steps.title: Execute ELISA assay
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of the diluted serum to each designated well of the microplate; incubate the plate at 37 °C for 25 minutes; wash the plate for five cycles, ensuring complete removal of liquid after each wash; add 100 µL of conjugate solution to each well and incubate again at 37 °C for 25 minutes; wash the plate for another five cycles; add 100 µL of TMB substrate to each well, protecting the plate from direct light; incubate for 10–15 minutes at room temperature while monitoring color development; add 50 µL of stop solution to each well to terminate the reaction; read the absorbance at 450 nm (applying any reference wavelength as indicated by the kit) within 30 minutes of adding the stop solution.

steps.title: Interpret ELISA results
steps.instruction: Calculate the optical density (OD) ratio or index according to the manufacturer’s instructions (typically sample OD divided by cut‑off control).

substeps.instruction: An OD ratio ≤ 0.90 is interpreted as negative.
An OD ratio between 0.91 and 1.09 is equivocal; repeat testing on the same or a new aliquot.
An OD ratio ≥ 1.10 is positive; perform confirmatory testing when available.
